introduction: Targeted at JEE Advanced and high-tier NEET questions, this level covers the complexities of Pure Rolling motion, conservation of angular momentum in dynamic systems, and the energetics of satellites and orbital mechanics.

core_concepts.title: Pure Rolling
core_concepts.description: A combination of translational and rotational motion where the relative velocity of the point of contact with the ground is zero ($v = \omega R$). The work done by static friction in pure rolling is zero.

core_concepts.title: Conservation of Angular Momentum Applications
core_concepts.description: If $\tau_{\text{ext}} = 0$, then $I_1 \omega_1 = I_2 \omega_2$. Example: When an ice skater pulls their arms in, their Moment of Inertia ($I$) decreases, causing their angular velocity ($\omega$) to increase drastically.

core_concepts.title: Gravitational Potential Energy ($U$)
core_concepts.description: The energy of a two-mass system is $U = -G(m_1 m_2)/r$. The negative sign is crucial; it indicates that the system is bound and work must be done to separate the masses.

core_concepts.title: Escape Velocity ($v_e$)
core_concepts.description: The minimum velocity required to project a body so it escapes the planet's gravitational pull completely: $v_e = \sqrt{2gR} \approx 11.2 \text{ km/s}$ for Earth.

core_concepts.title: Orbital Velocity ($v_o$)
core_concepts.description: The velocity required to keep a satellite in a circular orbit very close to the planet's surface: $v_o = \sqrt{gR} \approx 7.9 \text{ km/s}$ for Earth.

important_entities.name: Escape vs. Orbital Relationship
important_entities.significance: If an orbiting satellite's speed increases by $\sqrt{2}$ times (a 41.4% increase), it will break its orbit and escape into space.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive misconception is that friction always opposes motion in rolling. In pure rolling, static friction can act in the direction of motion to maintain the $v = \omega R$ constraint. Its direction depends purely on the external forces and torque.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For objects of the same mass and radius rolling down an incline: Solid Sphere > Disc > Hollow Sphere > Ring. The solid sphere reaches the bottom first because it has the lowest moment of inertia, translating more PE into linear KE.

exam_strategy_tips: In satellite energetics, memorize the relation: Kinetic Energy (KE) is positive, Potential Energy (PE) is negative, and Total Energy (TE) = PE/2 = -KE.
